quizzes.title: NEET-UG 2024 leak and the 2024 Act: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage: The NEET-UG 2024 controversy drew national attention after a paper leak was alleged in the examination. Alleged leak networks were reported in Patna and Hazaribagh, and the case showed how a question paper could be compromised before the test was held. Both places were linked to these alleged networks. Candidates in the examination were affected, and the controversy drew attention across the country. A group of candidates secured full marks, and the way those results were produced became a key point of dispute. Investigations later exposed organised cheating syndicates that had worked to compromise the examination process. Monitoring by the Supreme Court kept the case under close watch while the investigations continued. In response, Parliament passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act in 2024. The Act applies to major public examinations, including tests held by national-level recruitment and testing bodies. It is meant to deal with paper leaks, organised cheating and other forms of fraud connected with examinations. The law was therefore passed after the controversy had exposed these problems. The Act was thus a legal answer to the problems that the NEET-UG case had revealed. Its title shows that its focus is on unfair means in public examinations.

questions.q: Which bodies' examinations are covered by the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024?
options: UPSC, SSC, Railway Recruitment Boards, National Testing Agency and Institute of Banking Personnel Selection
questions.explanation: The text lists UPSC, SSC, Railway Recruitment Boards, National Testing Agency and Institute of Banking Personnel Selection as covered bodies.

questions.q: What aided the full-marks outcome in NEET-UG 2024 that intensified the controversy?
options: A revised answer key issued by a court
questions.explanation: The text says the full-marks outcome was aided by disputed grace marks.

questions.q: Alleged leak networks in the NEET-UG 2024 case were reported in which two states?
questions.explanation: The text places the reported networks in Patna (Bihar) and Hazaribagh (Jharkhand).

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 was India's first state-level law on paper leaks.
Reason (R): The Act is described as India's first dedicated central legislation on paper leaks, organised cheating and exam-related fraud.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
questions.explanation: The Act is a central law, so A is false, while R correctly describes it as India's first dedicated central legislation.

questions.q:
I. Parliament has passed an amendment to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act in 2026.
II. The full-marks outcome in NEET-UG 2024 was not connected to grace marks.
III. The full-marks outcome triggered nationwide protests and judicial scrutiny.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are stated in the text, while II is contradicted because the outcome was aided by disputed grace marks.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The NEET-UG paper leak controversy of 2026 intensified demands for stronger deterrence and faster legal proceedings.
II. The Act was enacted before the NEET-UG 2024 paper leak occurred.
III. The Act was enacted in 2026.
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since the Act was enacted in 2024 after the NEET-UG 2024 leak.

questions.q: How many candidates secured full marks in NEET-UG 2024?
questions.explanation: The text states that 67 candidates secured full marks.

quizzes.title: Special Task Force and task force reforms: MCQ practice
quizzes.passage: The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 followed a controversy over the NEET-UG 2024 examination, in which alleged paper leaks were reported in Patna and Hazaribagh. A group of candidates secured full marks in the same examination, and the outcome led to protests across the country. Investigations and monitoring by the Supreme Court followed. The Act is described as India's first dedicated central legislation on paper leaks, organised cheating and exam-related fraud. The Act covers major public examinations, including those conducted by UPSC and SSC. It includes a provision for a Special Task Force that can be set up to investigate offences under the law. Such a force is meant for specialised investigation and is linked to the Act's enforcement. The government has also constituted a high-powered task force to look into examination matters at a broader level. The high-powered task force is a separate body from the Special Task Force. The 2026 amendment, which Parliament has passed, adds further provisions to the framework created by the 2024 Act. The controversy that preceded the Act was widely followed, and the new provisions respond to demands for faster legal proceedings. Alleged leaks were the subject of investigation, and the NEET-UG case remained a reference point for the debate on examination fraud.

questions.q: Nandan Nilekani is a Co-Founder of which company?
questions.explanation: The text describes Nandan Nilekani as Co-Founder of Infosys.

questions.q: Nandan Nilekani is the Founding Chairman of which authority?
options: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
Securities and Exchange Board of India
questions.explanation: The text describes him as Founding Chairman of the Unique Identification Authority of India.

questions.q: The Special Task Force is particularly relevant to which kind of networks?
questions.explanation: The text ties the Special Task Force to inter-state paper-leak networks.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The high-powered task force was constituted to investigate individual offences under the Act.
Reason (R): The high-powered task force was constituted under Nandan Nilekani's chairmanship to drive strategic policy reforms.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
questions.explanation: Investigating offences is the role of the Special Task Force, so A is false, while R correctly describes the high-powered task force's mandate.

questions.q:
I. The Union Government is empowered to establish a Special Task Force for investigating offences under the Act.
II. The high-powered task force is chaired by Nandan Nilekani.
III. The Special Task Force is set up mainly to drive strategic policy reforms.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are stated in the text, while III wrongly assigns the policy-reform mandate to the Special Task Force.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The Special Task Force is particularly relevant to organised criminal syndicates.
II. The Special Task Force is particularly relevant only to offences committed within a single state.
III. Nandan Nilekani is a Co-Founder of Wipro.
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since the text links the force to inter-state networks and syndicates, not to a single state or to Wipro.

questions.q: Which authority is empowered to establish the Special Task Force under the Act?
questions.explanation: The text states that the Union Government is empowered to establish the Special Task Force.
